The discussion on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, exalted is He:

[45] ﴿So how many a town have We destroyed while it was wrongdoing, so it lies in ruins upon its roofs, and [how many] an abandoned well and a lofty palace.﴾

﴿So how many a town﴾ means: how many inhabitants of a town. ﴿We destroyed﴾ means: with punishment. ﴿While it was wrongdoing﴾ means: polytheistic and disbelieving. ﴿So it lies﴾ means: fallen. ﴿Upon its roofs﴾ means: its ceilings. ﴿And [how many] an abandoned well﴾ means: and how many a well was left unused, from which no water is drawn, because its people perished. ﴿And a lofty palace﴾ means: raised high. It comes from (shada al-binā'a), meaning he raised the building. Or its meaning is plastered and worked with al-shīd, with a kasra, which is gypsum plaster (al-jiss), meaning coated with plaster; we have emptied it of its residents. Among the evidence for the first meaning is the verse of ʿAdiyy ibn Zayd:

He built it of marble and coated it with lime, so for the birds there are nests on its heights.

(p-4349) The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, Exalted is He:

[46] ﴿Have they not travelled through the land, so that they might have hearts with which to understand, or ears with which to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind.﴾

﴿Have they not travelled﴾ i.e., the people of Makkah, in their trade, ﴿through the land, so that they might have﴾ i.e., through what they witness of the sources of admonition, ﴿hearts with which to understand﴾ i.e., what ought to be understood of monotheism (tawhid), ﴿or ears with which to hear﴾ i.e., what ought to be heard of revelation and warning. ﴿For indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind.﴾ The pronoun in (fa-innaha) refers to the matter (al-qissah). Or it is an ambiguous pronoun explained by (al-absar) [the eyes]. The meaning: the defect does not lie in their sense organs; rather it lies in their intellects, through following desire and immersion in heedlessness. The purpose of mentioning "the breasts" is emphasis, like His saying: ﴿they say with their mouths﴾ [Al 'Imran: 167] and ﴿a bird that flies with its two wings﴾ [Al-An'am: 38]; except that those are to affirm the literal meaning, whereas here it is to affirm the figurative meaning.

Al-Zamakhshari said: The purpose is the increase of depiction and definition. His expression: It is commonly known and believed that blindness in its literal sense has its place in the sight, namely that the pupil be struck by something that obliterates its light. Its use for the heart is a metaphor and a figure of speech. So when it is intended to establish what is contrary to the accepted belief, namely attributing blindness to the hearts literally and negating it from the eyes, this depiction needed additional specification and extra definition, so that it would be firmly established that the place of blindness is the hearts, not the eyes. As you say: "The keenness is not for the sword, but it is for your tongue that is between your two jaws." Your saying "that is between your two jaws" confirms and reinforces what you claimed for your tongue, because the locus of keenness is precisely that and nothing else. It is as if you said: I did not deny keenness from the sword and affirm it for your tongue by slip or inadvertence on my part, but I deliberately intended exactly that.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[47] ﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment, but Allah will never fail His promise. Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.﴾

﴿They ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, i.e., the punishment described in the verse: ﴿And when they said, "O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment."﴾ [al-Anfal: 32]. ﴿But Allah will never fail His promise﴾, i.e., He will certainly bring upon them what He has threatened them with, even if after some time. ﴿Indeed, a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾, i.e., He, exalted is He, is Forbearing (ḥalīm) and does not hasten. For the measure of a thousand years according to His creation is like one day with Him, in relation to His forbearance, since He knows that He is capable of retribution and that nothing escapes Him, even if He grants respite and gives time. For this reason He said after it:

The discussion concerning His saying, exalted is He:

[48] ﴿And how many a town did I give respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the final return.﴾

﴿And how many a town did I give respite﴾, i.e., I granted it a delay, ﴿while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the final return﴾, to My judgment is the return of all, so I will recompense them for their deeds. The connection of this verse with what precedes it is clear in explaining their error in the hastening mentioned, by showing the completeness of the breadth of His forbearance, exalted is He, and by manifesting the extreme narrowness of their disposition, which entails that the short period with Him, exalted is He, appears to them as long durations, as His saying, exalted is He, indicates: ﴿Indeed, they see it as far away﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 6] ﴿but We see it as near﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 7]. For this reason they regard its coming as distant, take it as a pretext for denying it, and presume to hasten it, not realizing that the measure by which all matters are estimated, both in occurrence and in report, is what is with Him, exalted is He, of extent. This was related by Ibn Kathir and Abu al-Su'ud.

In (al-'Inaya): When He mentioned their hastening, and explained that what they hastened would not fail to come, but was delayed out of forbearance, since a day with Him is a thousand years, what they considered long is not long in relation to Him; rather it is shorter than a day. It cannot be said: then the appropriate thing would be that a thousand years is like a day, and the reversal has no basis.

And al-Razi said: When He, exalted is He, related the magnitude of their disbelief, that they mock by hastening the punishment, He clarified that the intelligent person should not hasten the punishment of the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿And indeed, a day with your Lord﴾ [al-Hajj: 47], meaning in respect of the punishment they would receive and its severity: ﴿is like a thousand years﴾ [al-Hajj: 47], if counted in the abundance of pains and their intensity. Thus He, glorified is He, made clear that if they knew the state of the punishment of the Hereafter, and that it bears this description, they would not have hastened it.

Al-Razi said: This is the view of Abu Muslim, and it is the most preferable of the interpretations. End.

Al-Zamakhshari related it with his statement: It was said its meaning is: How do they hasten the punishment of One for whom a single day of the days of His punishment is, in length, a thousand years of your years? For the days of hardships are considered long, as it has been said:

Enjoy the days of happiness, for they are short, while the days of sorrows are long.

Or that single day, because of the severity of its punishment, is like a thousand years of the years of punishment. End.

Abu al-Su'ud adopted the first view, and he objected to what follows it, saying that neither the sublime context of the composition nor its setting supports it. For each of them indicates that the intended punishment is the worldly punishment, and that the extended time is that which passed over them before its arrival by way of respite and delay, not the time coinciding with it. Do you not see His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And how many a town﴾ etc., for it is explicit that what is meant is the swift, severe seizing after the long respite. End. And in it there is strength. And God knows best.

[49–51] ﴿Say: "O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you."﴾ ﴿So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision.﴾ [al-Hajj: 50] (p-4352) ﴿But those who strive against Our verses, seeking to cause them to fail, those are the companions of Hellfire.﴾ [al-Hajj: 51].

﴿Say: "O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you."﴾ ﴿So those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and noble provision.﴾ [al-Hajj: 50] This is Paradise. ﴿But those who strive against Our verses, seeking to cause them to fail, those are the companions of Hellfire.﴾ [al-Hajj: 51] That is: those who strive to repel Our verses and turn people away from them, opposing them. [52] ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he desired, Satan threw [something] into his desire. So Allah abolishes what Satan throws in; then Allah establishes His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.﴾

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet but that when he desired﴾ — i.e., he longed for the spread of his call and the swift elevation of his law. ﴿Satan threw [something] into his desire﴾ — i.e., with that which obstructs it and turns those being called away from answering it. ﴿So Allah abolishes what Satan throws in﴾ — i.e., He nullifies it and erases it. ﴿Then Allah establishes His verses﴾ — i.e., He confirms them. ﴿As for the scum, it passes away as refuse; but as for that which benefits people, it remains on the earth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17]. ﴿And Allah is Knowing﴾ — He knows the satanic throwings and the way of abrogating them from the aspect of His revelation. ﴿Wise﴾ — He establishes His verses with His wisdom. [53] ﴿That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened. Indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme opposition.﴾

**Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 22, verse 54 (part 1 of 4):**

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[54] ﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts humbly submit to it. And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path.﴾

﴿And that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts humbly submit to it﴾: that is, they submit with obedience and fear. The pronoun refers either to the Qur'an or to Allah, exalted is He. ﴿And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path﴾: that is, to the path of truth and uprightness, so that their feet do not slip by accepting what Satan casts, and their hearts accept only what the Most Merciful casts, because of their purity. This is the correct view in the tafsir (exegesis) of the verse. It has parallels that clarify its meaning, as we have indicated, if it needed a parallel. But it is clear in itself and needs no lengthy interpretation, were it not that it is necessary for the verifying scholars to refute what some transmitters have slipped in here of falsehoods. We will set out what has been said about it, then follow it with the critique of the verifying scholars, so that the reader is left with no need.

Ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: It has been said that the reason this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is that Satan had cast upon his tongue, in some of what he recited of what Allah had revealed to him of the Qur'an, something that Allah had not revealed to him. This grieved the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) greatly, and Allah consoled him for what he had suffered from it through these verses. Then he mentioned those who said this. He traced (the report) through an isnad (chain of narration) to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Muhammad ibn Qays and others, that: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sat in one of the assemblies of Quraysh, which had many people, and he wished on that day that nothing would come to him from Allah that would make them turn away from him. So Allah revealed to him: ﴿By the star when it descends﴾ [al-Najm: 1] ﴿Your companion has not strayed, nor has he erred﴾ [al-Najm: 2]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it until he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-Uzza﴾ [al-Najm: 19] ﴿And Manat, the third, the other one﴾ [al-Najm: 20]. Satan cast upon him two phrases: 'Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for.' He spoke them, then went on and recited the whole surah. He prostrated at the end of the surah, and all the people prostrated with him and were pleased with what he had said."

They said: When evening came, Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him and presented the surah to him. When he reached the two phrases mentioned, he said: "I did not bring you these two." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved. Then Allah, blessed and exalted is He, revealed to him, consoling him: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ [al-Hajj: 52], to the end of the verse."

Qadi 'Iyad said in (al-Shifa'): Know that we have two approaches in discussing the problematic aspects of this hadith: the first is to cast doubt on its foundation, and the second is to accept it for argument's sake.

As for the first approach, it suffices you that no one from among the people of sound transmission (ahl al-sihha) has recorded this, and no trustworthy narrator has related it with a sound, continuous isnad. It has been the preoccupation with this and its like of exegetes and historians who are devoted to every strange report, who snatch up from written pages every sound and unsound item. The Qadi Bakr ibn al-'Ala' al-Maliki spoke truly when he said: "People have been afflicted by some of the adherents of desires and of tafsir." The heretics have clung to this, despite the weakness of some of its transmitters, the disorder of its narrations, the interruption of its isnad, and the variation of its wording. As for those among the exegetes and the Successors (tabi'un) from whom this account is related, none of them traced it back to a chain of narration, nor raised it to a Companion. Most of the routes to them concerning it are feeble and weak. The only raised (marfu') report is the hadith of Shu'ba from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, as I think (the doubt is in the hadith), that the Prophet (ﷺ) was in Makkah, and he mentioned the story.

Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: We do not know this hadith to be related from the Prophet (ﷺ) by a continuous isnad that may be mentioned except this one. Only Umayya ibn Khalid transmitted it from Shu'ba, while others transmit it as mursal (with a missing Companion) from Sa'id ibn Jubayr. It is known only from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas. So Abu Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him, has made clear to you that it is not known through any route that may be mentioned other than this one. And in it there is the weakness he pointed out, together with the doubt in what we have mentioned, which cannot be relied upon and which carries no certainty. As for the hadith of al-Kalbi, it is not permissible to narrate it or mention it, because of the severity of its weakness and its falsity, as al-Bazzar, may Allah have mercy on him, indicated. What is authentically related of it is that: "The Prophet (ﷺ) recited the surah of al-Najm while he was in Makkah, and the Muslims, the polytheists, humans and jinn prostrated with him." This is its weakness from the standpoint of transmission.

As for the standpoint of meaning, the proof has been established, and the Ummah has agreed on his infallibility (ﷺ) and his freedom from such vileness. Either (i) he wished that something like this would descend upon him praising other than Allah, which is kufr (disbelief); or (ii) Satan would climb over him and make the Qur'an appear confused, so that he would insert into it what is not part of it, until Jibril (peace be upon them both) would alert him to it. All of this is impossible with regard to him (peace be upon him). Or (iii) the Prophet (ﷺ) would say that from himself deliberately, and that is kufr; or (iv) by mistake, and he is protected from all of this. A second point, which is the impossibility of this story by reason and custom: if the speech were as it is narrated, it would be far from coherent, contradictory in its parts, mixing praise with blame, and incoherent in its composition. The Prophet (ﷺ), those present with him of Muslims and the chieftains of the polytheists, would have been aware of it, and this is not hidden from even the least reflective person. How much more so for one whose forbearance is preponderant and whose knowledge in the field of eloquence and recognition of refined speech is vast!

A third point: it is known from the custom of the hypocrites, the stubborn polytheists, the weak-hearted and the ignorant among the Muslims, that they take fright at the very first moment, that the enemy confounds the Prophet (ﷺ) at the slightest trial, that they reproach the Muslims and gloat over them from time to time, and that whoever has a disease in his heart apostatizes from among those who showed Islam at the slightest doubt. No one has reported anything about this story except this narration whose foundation is weak. Had this happened, Quraysh would have found in it a great triumph over the Muslims, and the Jews would have used it to establish a proof against them, just as they stubbornly did in the matter of the Night Journey (isra'), until it became an apostasy for some of the weak. The same applies to what has been narrated about the affair of the 'Qadiyya' (the 'judgment' story). No trial would be greater than this calamity if it had occurred, and no agitation for the opponent would be stronger than this incident had it been possible. Yet no word was reported from any opponent concerning it, nor from any Muslim with a single word because of it. This indicates its falsehood and the uprooting of its basis. There is no doubt that some devils of humans and jinn have inserted it into the reports of some heedless narrators, to confuse the weak among the Muslims with it.

A fourth point: the transmitters mention for this affair that the following verses were revealed concerning it: ﴿And indeed, they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you﴾ [al-Isra': 73], and the two verses following. These two verses refute the report they have transmitted, because Allah, exalted is He, mentioned that they almost tempted him to fabricate against Him, and that had He not made him firm, he would almost have inclined toward them. The meaning and implication of this is that Allah protected him from fabricating and made him firm so that he did not incline toward them even a little, so how much less a great deal? Yet they narrate in their feeble reports that he went beyond inclining and fabricating, by praising their gods. This is the opposite of the meaning of the verse, and it weakens the hadith even if it were sound, so how much more so when it is not sound at all!

As for the second approach, it is based on accepting the hadith, if it were sound. Allah has preserved us from its soundness. Nevertheless, in any case, the imams of the Muslims have answered this with various responses, some weak and some strong. Among them is what Qatada and Muqatil have transmitted: that the Prophet (ﷺ) was overcome by drowsiness while reciting this surah, so these words came upon his tongue by the judgment of sleep. But this is not valid, since such a thing is not permissible for the Prophet (ﷺ) at any state of his, nor does Allah create it upon his tongue, nor does Satan gain mastery over him in sleep or wakefulness, given his infallibility in this matter from all deliberate and inadvertent error. He (peace be upon him) said: "Indeed my eyes sleep, but my heart does not sleep." In the hadith of al-Kalbi, the Prophet (ﷺ) spoke to himself, and Satan then said it upon his tongue. In the narration of Ibn Shihab from Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, he said: Among them, when he was informed of it, he said: "That is only from Satan." All of this is not valid to be said by him (peace be upon him), neither inadvertently nor intentionally, nor should Satan speak it on his tongue.

It has been said: Perhaps the Prophet (ﷺ) said it during his recitation, by way of reporting and rebuking the disbelievers, like the saying of Ibrahim: ﴿This is my Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 76], according to one of the interpretations, and like His saying: ﴿Rather, it was done by their biggest one, this one﴾ [al-Anbiya': 63], after a pause and a clear separation between the two speeches. Then he returned to his recitation. This is possible with a clear separation and an indication that points to the intended meaning, and that it is not part of what is recited. This is one of the things mentioned by the Qadi Abu Bakr (al-Baqillani).

Among what becomes apparent in its interpretation, if we grant the story, is that the 'cranes' (gharaniq) may refer to the angels, and hoping for intercession from the angels is correct. But when the polytheists interpreted it as meaning their gods, and Satan confused them with that, made it attractive in their hearts and cast it to them, Allah abrogated (naskh) what Satan had cast, established His verses, and removed the recitation of those two phrases. The words of the Qadi end here, summarized.

Abu Bakr al-Baqillani said: It has been said that he (ﷺ) used to recite the Qur'an in a measured manner (tartil), so Satan watched for him at one of the pauses (sakta) and uttered those words, imitating his melody, such that whoever drew near to him heard it and thought it was from his recitation of the Qur'an, and spread it.

He said: This is the best of the interpretations. It is supported by what is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he interpreted (tamanna, "wished") as (talā, "recited"). Ibn al-'Arabi also praised this interpretation. He had said before this: This verse is a clear text on the innocence of the Prophet (ﷺ) of what has been attributed to him, and that Satan added it to his words, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and not that he (peace be upon him) said it.

He said: Al-Tabari had already reached this view, endorsed this meaning, and hovered around it. Ibn al-'Arabi's praise of it is on the assumption that the story is sound; otherwise, he said: al-Tabari mentioned in this many numerous false narrations that have no basis. Taqi al-Din ibn Taymiyya said: There are two opinions on the verse, and what is transmitted from the early generation (salaf) agrees with the Qur'an in this. Those among the later scholars who denied this criticized what is transmitted of the addition in Surah al-Najm, with the words: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is indeed to be hoped for." They said: This has not been established. Whoever knows that it has been established says: This was cast by Satan into their ears, and the Messenger (ﷺ) did not utter it. But the question also arises on this assumption.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 22, verse 54 (part 2 of 4):

Some have said, regarding His words ﴿Except when he wishes, Satan casts into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj: 52], that it means "the talk of the self" (hadith al-nafs). Those who affirmed what has been transmitted from the early generations (al-salaf) said: "This has been transmitted by a firm transmission that cannot be impugned." They said: "The reports concerning the interpretation of this verse are well known and firmly established in the books of tafsir (Qur'anic exegesis) and hadith. The Qur'an agrees with this. For Allah's abrogation (naskh) of what Satan casts, and His making His verses firm (ihkam), only occurs to remove what came into His verses, and to distinguish truth from falsehood, so that His verses are not mixed with others. And the making of what Satan casts into a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease and whose hearts are hardened only occurs in a manner that is apparent, heard by the people, and not inward within the self. The trial that results from this type of abrogation is of the same kind as the trial that results from the other type of abrogation. Yet this type is more indicative of the truthfulness of the Messenger (ﷺ) and of his distance from desire than that type. For if he commands one matter and then commands its opposite, both being from Allah, and he is confirmed in that, then if he says about himself that the second is what is from Allah, and that it is the abrogating (nasikh), and that the thing abrogated by Allah is not so, he is more indicative of his reliance upon truthfulness and the speaking of truth. This is like what A'isha (may Allah be pleased with her) said: 'If Muhammad had been concealing anything of the revelation, he would have concealed this verse: ﴿And you concealed within yourself what Allah is to disclose, and you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him﴾ [al-Ahzab: 37].' Do you not see that one who magnifies himself with falsehood wants to defend everything he has said, even if it was an error? So the Messenger's (ﷺ) clarification that Allah made His verses firm and abrogated what Satan had cast is more indicative of his pursuit of truthfulness and his freedom from lying. This is the very purpose of the message, for he is the truthful, the one whose truthfulness is affirmed (ﷺ), with peace." End of quotation.

In his words, may Allah have mercy on him, there is scrutiny from several aspects:

First: his claim that the transmitted report agrees with the Qur'an. For this is a view that what Satan casts is cast into the verses. The verse does not indicate this, neither by direct correspondence (mutabaqa) nor by necessary implication (iltizam). Rather, saying so contradicts the revelation and the sending down (tanzil) as fire contradicts water, as you will see.

Second: his claim that the transmission of that narration is firmly established and cannot be impugned. Yet it has been impugned by countless scholars, both earlier and later. It suffices that his student, the memorizer (al-Hafiz) Ibn Kathir, said: "Many of the exegetes have mentioned here the story of the Gharaniq (the 'high-flying birds'). And there was the return of many of the emigrants to the land of Abyssinia, thinking that the polytheists of Quraysh had embraced Islam. But it comes through chains that are all mursal (with a missing companion in the isnad), and I have not seen it transmitted with a continuous chain (musnad) through any sound route. Counting its routes, after the weakness of its basis, is of no benefit. This is a doubt relied upon by many who stand with the narrations, thinking that a weak report grows stronger through the multiplicity of its routes, when in fact the weak remains weak however it comes. This doubt also crept into al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, so he began to strengthen some of its routes and to authenticate them from the side of the isnad, as you will see from his discussion. Had it had even the slightest trace of soundness, al-Bukhari would have included it as a mu'allaq (suspended report) or as a mawquf (ending with a companion), or the authors of the Sunan collections would have."

Third: his acknowledgment that the question arises on the assumption that the report is established, and that Satan cast that into their hearing. This demonstrates that the story contains flaws that reason rejects, just as the soundness of its transmissions rejects it.

Al-Fakhr al-Razi said in his tafsir: "This report is false and fabricated (mawdu'a) according to the people of verification (ahl al-tahqiq). They argued against it with the Qur'an, the Sunna, and reason. As for the Qur'an, there are several points:

The first: His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if he had fabricated against Us some sayings﴾ [al-Haqqa: 44] ﴿We would have seized him by the right hand﴾ [al-Haqqa: 45] ﴿then We would have severed his aorta﴾ [al-Haqqa: 46].

The second: His words: ﴿Say, It is not for me to change it of my own accord; I follow only what is revealed to me﴾ [Yunus: 15].

The third: His words: ﴿Nor does he speak from desire﴾ [al-Najm: 3] ﴿It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [al-Najm: 4].

The fourth: His words, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, to fabricate other than it against Us; and then they would have taken you as a friend﴾ [al-Isra: 73]. The word "kada" (almost) according to some of them means that it did not occur.

The fifth: His words: ﴿And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little﴾ [al-Isra: 74]. The word "lawla" (had it not been) indicates the non-existence of one thing due to the non-existence of another. So this indicates that that slight inclination did not take place.

The sixth: up to His words: ﴿Thus, that We may strengthen thereby your heart﴾ [al-Furqan: 32].

The seventh: His words: ﴿We will make you recite, so you will not forget﴾ [al-A'la: 6].

As for the Sunna, it is what is narrated from Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma, that he was asked about this story and said: 'This is a fabrication by the heretics (zanadiqa).' And he wrote a book on it."

The Imam Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Bayhaqi said: "This story is not established in terms of transmission." Then he began to speak about how the narrators of this story are impugned. Moreover, al-Bukhari narrated in his Sahih that "the Prophet, peace be upon him, recited Surat (al-Najm) and the Muslims, the polytheists, the humans and the jinn all prostrated in it." There is no mention of the story of the Gharaniq in it. And this hadith was narrated through many routes, and none of them at all contains the story of the Gharaniq.

As for reason, there are several points:

The first: whoever permits upon the Messenger (ﷺ) the glorification of idols has disbelieved, because it is known by necessity that the greatest of his striving was in negating idols.

The second: at the beginning of his mission he could not have prayed and recited the Qur'an at the Ka'ba safe from the harm of the polytheists throughout his call, to the extent that they sometimes stretched out their hands toward him. He only prayed, when they were not present, at night or at times of solitude. This refutes their claim.

The third: their enmity toward the Messenger was far too great for them to acknowledge this degree of recitation without seeking to know the reality of the matter. So how could they all agree that he glorified their gods, to the point that they fell down in prostration, when his agreement with them had not become apparent to them?

The fourth: His words: ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan casts; then Allah makes His verses firm﴾ [al-Hajj: 52]. For the making firm of the verses by removing what Satan casts from the Messenger is stronger than abrogating it with these verses, which leave doubt in place. So if Allah wants to make the verses firm, lest what is not Qur'an be confused with Qur'an, then that Satan be prevented from that altogether is more fitting.

The fifth, which is the strongest of the points: if we permitted that, the security of His law would be lifted, and we would permit in every one of the rulings and laws that it be likewise, and His words, exalted is He, would be nullified: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message; and Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 67]. For there is no difference in reason between a deficiency in the revelation and an addition to it. By these points we know, in summary, that this story is fabricated.

The most that can be said on this matter is that a group of exegetes mentioned it. But they did not reach the level of tawatur (mass transmission). And the report of a single transmitter does not oppose the rational and transmitted proofs that are mass-transmitted."

Then al-Razi extended the discussion of the topics at length, and he quoted from Abu Muslim al-Isfahani, in which the discussion expanded. Consult it if you wish.

The Ustadh al-Imam, the Mufti of Egypt, Shaykh Muhammad Abduh, may Allah have mercy on him, wrote an original essay on this verse, from which we quote some fragments.

He said: "Every reader of our Divine Book (the Qur'an) knows how highly Islam exalted the status of the prophets and messengers, and the rank that it granted them, as bearers of revelation and exemplars for humankind, in virtues and righteous deeds. And it exonerates them from what their enemies charged them with, and what the adherents of other religions attributed to them. It is not hidden from anyone of insight into this upright religion that it has affirmed the infallibility (ismah) of all the messengers from error in conveying the message, and from deviation from the direction toward which Allah turned their faces, in word or deed. And it singled out their seal, Muhammad (ﷺ), above that with merits explained throughout the Mighty Book. The infallibility of the messengers in conveying from Allah is a foundation of the principles of Islam. The Book bears witness to it, the Sunna supports it, and the Ummah has agreed upon it. What some sects differed on is other than reporting from Allah and conveying His revelation to His creation. This foundation, on which the religions rely, is a truth about which no adherent who understands the meaning of religion doubts. Yet falsehood has not been deprived of helpers who labor to demolish it and weaken its pillar. Those are the lovers of narrations (ushshaq al-ruwat) and the worshippers of transmission (abadat al-naql). They looked at His words, exalted is He: ﴿We did not send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ [al-Hajj: 52], and at what was narrated from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him and his father) that 'tamanna' means 'qara'a' (recited) and 'al-umniyya' means 'al-qira'a' (the recitation). Then the meaning of the interpretation became obscure to them, on the assumption that the report from Ibn Abbas is sound, so they went seeking what would make the interpretation valid in their view. Thereupon there arose for them someone who narrated in this regard hadiths whose routes differ, whose wordings vary, and which agree that the Prophet (ﷺ), when the harm of the polytheists reached him to the extent that it did, and they turned away from him, and his people and clan shunned him because of his criticism of their idols and his mockery of their gods, was overtaken by distress at their aversion. Out of eagerness for their conversion, he wished that nothing be sent down to him that would repel them, perhaps he would take that as a path to winning them over. So what he wished persisted until there was sent down to him Surat (al-Najm), to the end of what Ibn Jarir narrated first. Many of the exegetes have followed him in this. In human nature is the familiarity with the strange and the eagerness for the marvelous. So they became enamored of these tafsirs and forgot what the majority of the verifying scholars saw in its interpretation and what the imams adopted in its explanation.

It is stated in Sahih al-Bukhari: 'Ibn Abbas said regarding: ﴿When he wishes, Satan casts into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj: 52]: "When he speaks, Satan casts into his speech, and then Allah nullifies what Satan casts and makes His verses firm." And it is said: "His umniyya (wish) is his recitation": ﴿except wishes (amani)﴾ [al-Baqara: 78], they recite but do not write.' End of quotation.

So you see that he related the interpretation of umniyya as recitation with the phrase 'yuqal' (it is said), after he had interpreted it as speech through a report from Ibn Abbas. This indicates a difference between the two interpretations. What the commentators claim, that speech in Ibn Abbas's view means recitation, contradicts the apparent wording. Then reporting the interpretation of umniyya as the meaning of recitation with the phrase 'yuqal' indicates that it is not considered authoritative by him. And it will come that what is meant by speech is the talk of the self (hadith al-nafs).

Abu al-Ibriz said: 'The interpretation of "tamanna" as "qara'a" and of "al-umniyya" as "al-qira'a" is reported from Ibn Abbas in the version of Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas. And Ali ibn Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, narrated it from Mu'awiya ibn Salih from Ali ibn Abi Talha from Ibn Abbas. And it is known what people have said about Ibn Abi Salih, the scribe of al-Layth, and that the verifiers are upon his weakening.' End of quotation.

This is what is in the report from Ibn Abbas, and it is the origin of this trial. I have seen that the verifiers weaken its narrator. As for the story of the Gharaniq, despite what differences there are in it, many imams have criticized it, to the extent that Ibn Ishaq said: 'It is from the fabrications of the heretics,' as has preceded from al-Razi, and similarly from the Qadi Iyad, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding its feebleness and its collapse from several aspects."

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 22, verse 54 (part 3 of 4):

As for what Ibn Hajar mentioned, that the story was narrated in mursal (disconnected) reports through routes that meet the conditions of the sound (sahih), and that those who accept the mursal as evidence may rely on it, he has erred in this, as he himself said in al-Ibriz: infallibility (al-'ismah) is among the articles of belief in which certainty is required. A report that aims to undermine and nullify it is not accepted in any form in which it comes. The jurists of legal theory (al-usuliyyun) have counted a report of this kind among those reports whose falsity must be asserted with certainty. This is the case even if the chain of narration were connected, so what do you think of disconnected reports? The disagreement over accepting or rejecting the mursal concerns matters of practice and the branches of rulings, not the foundations of belief and the core of faith. The mursal reports that have come from them concern those things. This is a lapse by Ibn Hajar, may Allah forgive him for it.

This is what the Imams, may Allah reward them with good, have said in explaining the corruption of this story and that it has no basis. No weight is given to the opinion of those who disagree with them. Its mention in some books of tafsir should not be relied upon, however famous its authors may have been. The fame of the one in error does not add strength to his statement, nor should it be taken as a reason to adopt his opinion.

Then the Ustadh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Now I return to the interpretation of the verses in the manner that their wording permits and their expressions indicate. And Allah knows best.

It is not hidden from anyone who understands the Arabic language and has read some of the Qur'an that the words of His, exalted is He, ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ [al-Hajj: 52] and what follows, describe a decree that was ordained for all the messengers, which they do not transgress and beyond which they do not stop. It describes a characteristic that was known of them and of their nations. If what those exegetes said were correct, the meaning would be that Satan had been empowered over all the prophets and messengers, and he confused the revelation sent down to them. Then, after this confusion, Allah abrogates the speech of Satan and makes His verses firm, and so on. This is among the most repugnant things one could imagine concerning Allah's choosing of His prophets and selecting them from among His special friends! Let us leave this nonsense and return to what we are concerned with.

* *

Allah mentioned to His Prophet a condition of the prophets and messengers before him, in order to explain to him His way with them. This follows His saying, ﴿And if they deny you, then the people of Noah, and 'Ad and Thamud, had denied [their messengers] before them﴾ [al-Hajj: 42], up to the end of the verses. Then He said, ﴿Say: O mankind, I am to you only a clear warner﴾ [al-Hajj: 49]. ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them is forgiveness and noble provision﴾ [al-Hajj: 50]. ﴿But those who strive against Our verses, seeking to cause failure, they are the companions of the Hellfire﴾ [al-Hajj: 51]. ﴿Never did We send before you any messenger or prophet﴾ [al-Hajj: 52], and so on. So the preceding narratives concerned the denial of the nations toward their prophets. Then there followed the divine command that the Prophet (ﷺ) say to his people: I have only been sent to you to warn you of the consequence of what you are upon, and to give good tidings of bliss to the believers. As for those who strive against the signs and proofs that I have established as guidance and as paths to felicity, in order to turn attention away from them, to veil them from sight, to corrupt their effect for which they were established, and to make the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers unable to prevail, that is, they compete with them in order to overcome them and silence them from speaking of it, by playing with words and turning them away from the intent of the one who uttered them, as is customary among people of disputation and obstinacy: these misguided misleaders are the companions of the Hellfire. Then He followed this with what indicates that what the Prophet (ﷺ) was tested with in the form of opposition in the signs, the earlier prophets were also tested with. No prophet was sent to a nation without having opponents who harmed him through distortion and misinterpretation, who opposed his hopes, and who stood between him and what he sought, by placing obstacles in his path. In light of this meaning, which agrees with what all the prophets encountered, the verse must be interpreted. This occurs in two ways:

(p. 4366) The first: that (tamanna) means (qara'a), "recited," and (al-umniyyah) means (al-qira'ah), "recitation." This is a meaning that may be valid, and the word has been used in this sense. Hassan ibn Thabit said about Uthman, may Allah be pleased with them both:

"He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of its night
and at its end, and met the fate decreed by destiny."

Another poet said:

"He recited the Book of Allah at the beginning of its night
like David reciting the Psalms at his leisure."

However, the (ilqa', "casting") does not mean what they mentioned. Rather, it means what is understood from your saying, "I slipped into the speech of so-and-so," when you introduce into it something its wording may bear but which he did not intend, or when you attribute to him what he did not say, under the pretext that this speech leads to it. This is the work of the obstructers who set themselves up to fight the truth, who follow doubt and pursue suspicion. Thus casting in this sense is their habit. The attribution of casting to Satan is because he is the one who stirs up doubts with his whisperings and corrupts hearts with his intrigues. Whatever proceeds from the people of misguidance may rightly be attributed to him. The meaning would be: We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that, when he spoke to his people about his Lord, or recited a revelation sent down to him for their guidance, obstinate opponents stood up against him, distorting what he recited to them from its intended meaning, attributing to him what he did not say, and spreading that among the people in order to alienate them from him and divert them from his path. Then Allah establishes the truth and nullifies falsehood. The prophets continued to be patient over what they were denied and harmed by, and they struggled for the truth. They did not regard as significant the efforts of those who tried to defeat them, nor the mockery of the mockers, until the truth prevailed through striving and triumphed over falsehood through struggle. Thus Allah abrogates those doubts and uproots them from their foundations, and establishes and confirms His verses. Allah has set this way among people so that the evil may be distinguished from the good. Those in whose hearts is a disease, who are weak in intellect, are tried by those doubts and whisperings, and so they pursue them. Those whose hearts are hardened among the people of obstinacy and denial are also tried by them, and they take them as a support upon which to rely in their disputation. Then the truth becomes clear to those who have been given knowledge, and it becomes pure for them after every doubt has come upon it. They know that it is the truth from your Lord, so they believe in it, and their hearts humble themselves and find peace in it. Those who have been given knowledge are those who have been granted the capacity to distinguish between the decisive proof that settles in the intellect at the depth of certainty, and between sophistries and kinds of sophistry that drive understanding astray and carry it away with illusion, taking the intellect now to the left and now to the right.

Whether you take the pronoun in (that it is the truth) to refer to what the clear, decisive verses of divine guidance have brought, or to the Qur'an itself, which is the most exalted of them, the meaning is valid according to what those who have been established in knowledge hold. These people who have been given knowledge are those who believed. They are the ones Allah guided to the straight path, and He has not given illusion any authority over them, so that it would turn them away from that upright way. As for those who disbelieved, who are weak in intellect and sick in heart, or who are the people of obstinacy, the leaders of falsehood, and the hard-natured, whose hearts do not soften and do not yield to the truth, they remain in doubt about the truth or the Book. Their intellects do not settle upon it, and they do not refer to it in the conduct of their affairs, until the hour of their destruction comes suddenly, and they meet their reckoning with their Lord. Or if the time extends for them and their term is prolonged, then the torment of a barren day will befall them: a day of war in which they will be made to taste the worst torment, killing or capture. They will be cast into places of humiliation and abodes of evil. From that day nothing good or blessing will come to them. Rather, what they had will be taken from them, and they will be driven to places of ruin. This is barrenness in its fullest sense and its most wretched degree. How close these verses are in their meanings to His, exalted is He, saying in Surah Al 'Imran: ﴿He is the One who has sent down to you the Book; in it are verses that are precise, which are the foundation of the Book, and others that are allegorical. As for those in whose hearts is deviation, they follow what is allegorical in it, seeking discord and seeking its interpretation. And no one knows its interpretation except Allah. And those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord." And none will be reminded except those of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 7]. He then said after that: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve, their wealth and their children will not avail them against Allah at all, and they are the fuel of the Fire﴾ [Al 'Imran: 10], then He said: ﴿Say to those who disbelieve, "You will be overcome and gathered to Hell, and wretched is the resting place"﴾ [Al 'Imran: 12], and so on through the verses. (p. 4368) It is as if one of the two passages of the Qur'an explains the other. Those in whose hearts is deviation are those in whose hearts is disease, and whose hearts are hardened. Those firm in knowledge are those who have been given knowledge, and these are the ones who know that it is the truth from their Lord. So they say, "We believe in it; all of it is from our Lord," and their hearts humble themselves to it. And indeed, Allah is the One who guides them to a straight path. Those are the ones who are tried by interpretation, and who occupy themselves with "it was said" and "it was said," with what Satan casts, and he turns them away from the targets of clear exposition and inclines them away from the clear path of the Criterion. As for what they rely upon of wealth and children, it will not avail them against Allah at all. Their appointed terms will reach them, and their deeds will meet them. If their term does not reach them upon their beds, they will be overcome in their conflict. This is the way of all the prophets with their nations, and the path of truth against falsehood since the day Allah raised man to a station in which he distinguishes between his happiness and his misery, and between what preserves him and what takes away his existence. Just as there is no place for the story of the Gharaniq (the "Satanic verses" tradition) in the verses of Al 'Imran, there is no place for it in the verses of Surah al-Hajj. This is the first way of interpreting the verses ﴿Never did We send﴾ [al-Hajj: 52] to their end, on the assumption that (tamanna) means (qara'a) and that (al-umniyyah) means (al-qira'ah). And Allah knows best.

The second interpretation (wajh) regarding the meaning of the verses: that tamanni (تَمَنِّي, "wishing/desiring") is in its well-known meaning. Likewise umniyyah (أُمْنِيَّة, "wish, desire"), which is of the pattern ufu'ulah in the sense of al-munyah (المُنْيَة). Its plural is amani (أمانِيّ), as is well known. Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya said: tamanni is the soul's discourse about what will happen and what will not happen. He said: and tamanni is asking the Lord. And in a hadith: "If one of you wishes (tamanna), let him increase (his wishing), for he is only asking his Lord," and in another narration: "let him increase it." Ibn al-Athir said: tamanni (تَمَنِّي) is the longing for the attainment of a desired matter, and the soul's discourse about what will and what will not happen. Abu Bakr said: "I tamannaytu the thing" when I measure it and love that it should come to me. Everything that has been said about the meaning of tamanni in this sense returns to what we have mentioned, and the meaning of umniyyah follows it.

No messenger or prophet has been sent by God to call a people to a new guidance, or to a previously prescribed law which He had laid down for them, and to move them to affirm a book brought by himself if he was a messenger, or brought by another if he was a prophet sent to lead people to follow one who preceded him, except that he has an umniyyah among his people. It is that they follow him (p-4369) and incline to what he calls them to, seek healing from their disease through his remedy, and defy their desires by answering his call. There is no messenger who was sent except that he was most eager for the faith of his community and their affirmation of his message, more than his food that he eats, his drink that he drinks, and his dwelling to which he turns. He goes out from them and returns to us. Our Prophet ﷺ was of this in the highest station and the loftiest place. God Most High said: ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief over their traces if they do not believe in this discourse﴾ [al-Kahf: 6]. He said: ﴿And most of the people, even if you were eager, would not be believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103]. He said: ﴿Would you compel the people until they become believers?﴾ [Yunus: 99]. And there is in the verses what would take long to enumerate, which indicates his ﷺ umniyyat concerning the guidance of his people and bringing them out of the darknesses they were in, into the light of what he brought. There is no messenger or prophet except that when he wishes this lofty umniyyah, Satan casts stumbling blocks in his path and sets obstacles between him and his goal. He whispers into the breasts of people and deprives them of benefiting from what they were given of the power of reason and perception, so they rise up against him, turn him away from his purpose, and frustrate him, until they may frustrate him; and they dispute with him by the sword and by speech, until they may overpower him. When they prevail over him, while the call is in its beginning, and it is easy for them to harm him while he has few followers and weak helpers, they think the truth is on their side, and what they cast of obstacles between him and what he aimed at becomes a trial for them.

The sunnah of God has prevailed that the messengers be from the midst of their peoples, or from among the weak among them, so that the factor in submitting to the truth is purely evidence and the strength of proof. And so that free choice is what moves those called to accept it. And lest truth share with falsehood in its means, or share with it in setting its snares and nets. The supporters of falsehood in every age are the people of arrogance, strength, rank, and self-importance through wealth, children, clan, helpers, and delusion through adornments, and pride in the abundance of knowledge. (p-4370) These qualities, all or some of them, gather in leaders and people of standing, distracting them from themselves and diverting their gaze from the path of their guidance. When a caller calls to the truth, pure hearts recognize it, free from the filth of these trials, and pure souls and minds prepared to accept it turn to it, being free of these preoccupations. Such hearts are rarely found except among the weak and the humble. When these gather around the caller and support him in his call, those deluded ones rise and say: ﴿We do not see you but as a human like ourselves, and we do not see that those who follow you are except our lowest, immature in judgment, and we see in you no superiority over us; rather, we think you are liars﴾ [Hud: 27]. When God lets them be drawn on by His sunnah, and makes the contest between them and the believers alternate in turns, those in whose hearts there is sickness among their adherents are tried, and they too are tried by what they gain of victory in their defense. But God is dominant over His affair. He then obliterates what Satan cast of these doubts, removes these hindrances and those obstacles, and the authority rises for His signs, establishing them and fixing their pillars, producing strength from the weakness of their helpers, and giving them honor in place of their humiliation; and the word of God becomes the highest and the word of Satan the lowest: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum, but what benefits the people remains on the earth﴾ [al-Ra'd: 17]. In relating this divine sunnah upon which He established the prophets and messengers, there is consolation for our Prophet ﷺ regarding what he encountered from his people, and a promise that He will complete his religion for him and perfect His favor upon him and upon the believers, while directing their attention to the example of those who preceded them: {﴿Do the people think that they will be left to say, "We believe," and they will not be tried?﴾ [al-Ankabut: 2] ﴿And We did certainly try those before them, and God will surely know those who are truthful and will surely know the liars﴾ [al-Ankabut: 3]}, ﴿Or do you think you will enter Paradise while there has not yet come to you the example of those who passed before you? They were touched by misfortune and adversity and were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the victory of God?" Unquestionably, the victory of God is near﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214].

This is the second interpretation of the meaning of the verse. It is indicated by the preceding verses, and it guides to the context of the previous narratives in His saying: ﴿And if they deny you, then indeed the people of Noah denied before them﴾ [al-Hajj: 42], etc. You see that the story of the cranes (al-gharaniq) does not agree with this correct meaning.

There is a third interpretation mentioned by the author of al-Ibriz, and I quote it verbatim, and it is not far from this at all. He said: (after mentioning the prophets' umniyyat for their communities, and their hope for their faith, and the matter of our Prophet ﷺ in that, in a manner close to what we mentioned in the second interpretation):

Then the community differs, as God Most High said: ﴿But they differed: among them were those who believed and among them were those who disbelieved﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253]. As for those who disbelieve, Satan has cast into them the whisperings that undermine their acceptance of the message and necessitate their disbelief. Likewise the believer also is not free from whisperings, for they are generally inseparable from belief in the unseen, though they differ among people in quantity and quality, and according to what they are attached to. When this is established, the meaning of (tamanna) is that he wishes for them faith, and loves for them good, guidance, righteousness, and success. This is the umniyyah of every messenger and prophet. Satan's casting into it occurs by what he casts into the hearts of the community of the call of whisperings that necessitate the disbelief of some of them. God has mercy on the believers and abrogates that from their hearts, and establishes in them the verses that indicate the oneness and the message, and keeps that, Mighty and Majestic, in the hearts of the hypocrites and disbelievers so that they may be tried by it. Thus it emerges from this that whisperings are first cast into the hearts of both groups together, but they do not persist among the believers and persist among the disbelievers. End.

When you examine between this explanation and what preceded it, you will discern which is more worthy of preference. If what the transmitters of the story of the cranes said were sound, trust in revelation would be lost and reliance upon it would be broken, as al-Qadi al-Baydawi and others said. And the discourse about the abrogating would be like the discourse about the abrogated; it would be permissible for Satan to cast into it whatever he wishes, and the greatest pillar of the divine laws, which is infallibility (al-'ismah), would collapse. What is said in way of escape from that is repugnant to taste and the intellect does not accept it. Moreover, the description of the Arabs of their gods as "the exalted cranes" did not occur in their poetry or their speeches, and it was not reported from anyone that this description was current on their tongues, except what came in Mu'jam Yaqut without a chain of transmission and without being known through a sound path. This indicates that the story is a fabrication of the zanadiqa (heretics), as Ibn Ishaq said. Perhaps it was the source of what Yaqut reported. It is not hidden that gharnuq and gharniq are not known in the language except as the name of a water bird, black or white, or the name of the crane or a bird resembling it; and gharniq (with a damma, and like zunbur, qindil, samaw'al, firdaws, qirtas, and 'ulabit) means a young man, white and beautiful. The twisted lock of hair is called gharnuq, as a kind of tree is also so named. Gharnuq and gharaniq are applied to what is in the base of the soft-growing 'awsaj (a shrub). It is said: "lummah gharanqah" and "gharaniqiyyah," meaning soft, shaded by the wind; or gharnuq is the soft plant hidden among vegetation, etc. None of these meanings suits gods and idols, so as to be applied to them in eloquent speech presented to the kings of eloquence and the princes of speech. So I do not think you believe otherwise than that they are fabrications of the non-Arabs and inventions of the deceivers, of those who cannot distinguish between free speech and what has been enslaved of it for weak minds. This was accepted by those whom the eagerness for narration distracts from what understanding requires: ﴿Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us from Yourself mercy. Indeed, You are the Bestower﴾ [Al 'Imran: 8]. End of the words of the Ustadh, may God have mercy on him.

Among those who categorically asserted the fabrication of this story is the Imam Ibn Hazm, may God have mercy on him, where he said in his book "al-Milal," in refuting those who did not require infallibility for the prophets, something to this effect: They argued with the lying hadith that never was authentic in his peace be upon him reciting: ﴿By the star when it descends﴾ [al-Najm: 1], and they mentioned that fabricated addition, resembling its fabricator, saying: "And indeed they are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for." Then he said afterward: As for the hadith in which there are the cranes, it is pure falsehood, fabricated, for it was never authentic through any chain of transmission, and there is no point in occupying oneself with it, since fabricating a lie is something no one is incapable of. As for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he wished, Satan cast into his wish﴾ [al-Hajj: 52], etc., there is no argument for them in it. For the wishes that occur in the soul have no meaning. The Prophet ﷺ wished for the Islam of his uncle Abu Talib (p-4373) and God Mighty and Majestic did not will that to occur. So these are the wishes that God Mighty and Majestic mentioned, and no others, and far be it from God that a prophet should wish for disobedience. And success is from God.

What we have said is the apparent meaning of the verse without excessive strain, and it is not permissible to depart from the apparent meaning except by another apparent meaning. And success is from God Most High. End. And His saying, Most High:

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[55] ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾, i.e., in doubt and dispute concerning the Noble Revelation, because of what has been sealed upon their hearts. ﴿Until the Hour comes upon them﴾, i.e., the Resurrection, ﴿suddenly﴾, i.e., unexpectedly. ﴿Or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day﴾, i.e., a day after which there is no day. As if every day gives birth to the days that follow it, so a day after which there is no day is barren. What is meant by it is also the Hour. As if it were said: "or its punishment comes upon them," and that was put in the place of its pronoun for greater awe. Abu al-Su'ud conveyed this. That is, because it means: severe, having no like in its severity.

Previously, in what we quoted, there was another aspect: the meaning is that those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about the truth or the Book, their minds not settling upon it, until the moment of their destruction comes suddenly, and they meet their reckoning before their Lord. Or, if time extends for them and their term prolongs their span, then there will befall them the punishment of a barren day: a day of war in which they are made to taste the evil punishment of killing or capture. No good or blessing will issue for them from that day. Rather, they will be stripped of what they possessed and driven to the places of destruction. This is barrenness in its most complete meaning and its most ominous degree. End of quote.

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[56] ﴿The dominion on that Day belongs to Allah; He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss.﴾

(p-4374) ﴿The dominion on that Day﴾, i.e., the Day when their doubt vanishes. ﴿Belongs to Allah﴾, i.e., alone, such that no one has any disposal whatsoever, neither in reality nor in appearance. ﴿He will judge between them﴾, i.e., by recompense. Then he explained the judgment by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss.﴾

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[57–59] ﴿As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah, then were killed or died, Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers﴾ [al-Hajj: 58] ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing﴾ [al-Hajj: 59].

﴿As for those who disbelieve and deny Our signs, for them is a humiliating punishment﴾ ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah, then were killed﴾ [al-Hajj: 58], meaning in jihad, ﴿or died, Allah will surely provide for them a good provision﴾ [al-Hajj: 58], meaning from Paradise and its bounties, ﴿And indeed, Allah is the best of providers﴾ [al-Hajj: 58]. ﴿He will surely admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. And indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing﴾ [al-Hajj: 59].

Al-Qasimi said in al-Iklil (Kitab al-Iklil fi Istinbat al-Tanzil): Fadalah ibn Ubayd al-Ansari, the Companion, used as evidence His saying, ﴿then were killed or died﴾ [al-Hajj: 58], for the view that the one who is killed and the one who dies in the way of Allah are equal in merit. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. This is an opinion held by a group of scholars. Others disagreed with him and preferred the one who is killed. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Sulayman, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever dies while stationed on the frontier (murabitan), Allah will grant him the like of that reward, and will continue to provide for him, and he will be safe from the tempters (al-fattanin). And recite, if you wish: ﴿And those who emigrated in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 58] up to: ﴿Forbearing﴾ [al-Hajj: 59]."

The discussion concerning the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[60] ﴿That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, then is wronged again, Allah will surely help him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾

(p-4375) ﴿That is so. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was afflicted with, then is wronged again, Allah will surely help him﴾ That is: whoever repays a wrongdoer in measure with his wrong, without exceeding in the retaliation against him, and then the wrongdoer transgresses against him a second time, Allah will surely help that wronged person. The initiation of punishment, which is in fact a requital, has been named "punishment" for the sake of pairing (ijdiwaj, i.e. balance of wording) and correspondence (mushakalah, i.e. verbal correspondence). Or it is because it is the cause of the requital. And in His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ there is an allusion (ta'rid) urging pardon and forgiveness. For He, exalted is He, despite the perfection of His power, pardons and forgives, so others are more deserving of that. And it is an alert to His power to help, since only one who is able to do the opposite is described as pardoning. Thus the secret of the correspondence between "Pardoning" and "Forgiving" to this context becomes apparent.

The discussion on the interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying:

[61–62] ﴿That is because Allah causes the night to enter into the day, and causes the day to enter into the night, and because Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ ﴿That is because Allah is the Truth, and because what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ [Al-Hajj: 62].

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted:

﴿Have you not seen that Allah sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Aware.﴾ ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 22, verse 67:

The discussion of the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying:

[67] ﴿For every community We have appointed a rite (mansak) which they perform, so let them not dispute with you about the matter, and invite to your Lord; indeed, you are upon right guidance, straight.﴾

﴿For every community We have appointed﴾, i.e., We have placed; ﴿a rite (mansak)﴾, i.e., a sacred law (shari'ah) and a means of worship; ﴿which they perform, so let them not dispute with you about the matter﴾, i.e., about that appointing and placing, and the argument over its diversity among every community and its lack of unity; or about the matter of what you have brought them, on the claim that it can dispense with what was legislated before it. For that is ignorance of His wisdom, exalted is He, in shaping the nations and training them through laws suited to their time and place, their life and their origin. For this reason this law (shari'ah) was the most rightly guided of the laws, for the blessing of it, when mankind reached the highest stage of maturity. For this reason calling to it became obligatory in particular, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿and invite to your Lord; indeed, you are upon right guidance, straight﴾, i.e., remain firm in your religion with a steadfastness that leaves them no hope of deceiving you concerning it. Or its meaning is: persevere in calling to what you have been commanded, so their disputing will not harm you. In all cases, following you and not opposing you is incumbent upon them, since the matter is settled upon your law (shari'ah), for it is the straight path.

That said, Ibn Jarir said: The root of mansak (rite) in the speech of the Arabs is the customary place that a man frequents and is accustomed to, for good or for ill. It is said: "So-and-so has a mansak he frequents," meaning a place he visits and is accustomed to, for good or ill. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of "nusk" (rite) here: it was said, a festival; and it was said, the shedding of blood. [Ibn Jarir] then favored that the meaning is the shedding of blood on the days of sacrifice at Mina, because the rites about which the polytheists disputed with the Messenger of God (ﷺ) were the shedding of blood on these days. That is, these polytheists should not dispute with you about your slaughter and your rite by saying: "Do you eat what you kill, and not eat what God has killed?" End of quote.

Accordingly, the intended meaning of "appointed" in His saying ﴿We have appointed﴾ is the appointing by divine decree, not by legislation, as He said: ﴿And for each there is a direction which he faces﴾ [al-Baqarah: 148], i.e., they only do this by God's decree and will. So do not be affected by their disputing with you, and let that not divert you from the truth you are upon. This is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let them not turn you away from the signs of God after they have been sent down to you; and invite to your Lord﴾ [al-Qasas: 87]; Ibn Kathir pointed this out. Al-Razi transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas, in the narration of 'Ata', that the intended meaning of mansak is the sacred law (shari'ah), the method (minhaj). He said: This is the choice of al-Qaffal, based on His saying: ﴿For each of you We have appointed a law (shir'ah) and a method (minhaj)﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 48]. This is what we preferred first, for its clarity in it. And God knows best.

(p-4379) The explanation of His saying, the Exalted:

[72–74] ﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them, you will recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve. They nearly assault those who recite Our verses to them. Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve. And wretched is the destination."﴾ ﴿O mankind, a parable is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for that. And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not recover it from it. Weak are the seeker and the sought.﴾ [al-Hajj: 73] ﴿They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.﴾ [al-Hajj: 74].

﴿When Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, i.e., while they are evident in their indication of their truth and what they contain. ﴿you will recognize denial in the faces of those who disbelieve﴾, i.e., the denial, or the monstrous aspect of aggression and scowling, or the evil they intend, appearing through its signs. ﴿They nearly assault those who recite Our verses to them﴾, i.e., they nearly lash out at them out of excessive rage and anger. Al-Nisaburi said in (Fath al-Bayan): "Likewise the people of misguided innovations: when one of them hears what the scholar recites to him from the verses of the Glorious Book or from the authentic Sunnah, contrary to the falsehood he believes, you see in his face such denial that, if he were able to lash out with it, he would do to them what he would not do to the polytheists." And Allah casts the truth upon falsehood, so it crushes it, and behold, it vanishes. ﴿Say: "Shall I inform you of something worse than that? The Fire, which Allah has promised to those who disbelieve. And wretched is the destination."﴾

﴿O mankind, a parable is presented﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., it is made clear. ﴿a parable﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., a strange condition. ﴿so listen to it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., reflect upon it with true reflection, for listening without reflection and understanding does not benefit. ﴿Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], meaning the idols. ﴿will never create a fly, even if they gathered together for that﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., to create it, cooperating. Their specifying the fly is for its lowliness, its weakness, and its repulsiveness. This is among the most eloquent of what was revealed in exposing the ignorance of the polytheists, in that they are described with divinity, which requires power over all capable things and comprehensive knowledge of all knowable things, while they are mere images and statues, which cannot possibly create even the least and most abased of what Allah the Exalted has created, even if they gathered for that. ﴿And if the fly should snatch away from them anything, they could not recover it from it﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., this creature, the least and most abased, if it snatched something from them, and they gathered together to retrieve it from it, they would not be able to. ﴿Weak are the seeker﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., the idol seeking what was taken from it. ﴿and the sought﴾ [al-Hajj: 73], i.e., the fly with what it took. This is like equating them with the fly in weakness. Yet if you examine it closely, you will find the seeker weaker and weaker still, for the fly is a living creature while the idol is inanimate. The one who prevails is the fly, and that which is overcome is the idol.

It is also permissible that by "the seeker" is meant the worshipper of the idol, and by "the sought" is meant the one he worships. It was said: this is more appropriate to the context, since it serves to expose their ignorance and belittle what they worship, and so it suits the intent of the concluding statement regarding the idols. Al-Zamakhshari chose the first interpretation, because it contains mockery, by presenting the idol as a seeker for the sake of supposition, mocking it, and because it is weaker than the fly, being snatched from and inanimate, whereas the fly is a living creature, unlike it.

This concluding statement is either information or an expression of wonder. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿They have not appraised Allah with His true appraisal﴾ [al-Hajj: 74], i.e., they did not know Him with true knowledge, in that they associated with Him what cannot even defend itself against a fly or obtain justice from it. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾ [al-Hajj: 74], i.e., able and dominant. How then can the weak and vanquished be taken as His likeness? Or: He is powerful by the support of His allies, and Exalted in Might, He takes vengeance upon His enemies.
