The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[75–76] ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah are all matters returned.﴾ [al-Hajj: 76].

﴿Allah chooses﴾, i.e., selects: ﴿messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾. That is, there is no denial of His choosing from among humans whomever He wills for His message. And there is no basis for their saying: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ [Sad: 8]. Abu al-Su'ud said: It is as if the Exalted, when He established His oneness in divinity and negated that anything among things could share in it, made clear that He has servants chosen for the message, through whose responding and being followed one reaches the worship of Him, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Baydawi preceded him with something similar. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Hajj: 76], i.e., what they have done and what they will do. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾ [al-Hajj: 76], i.e., because He is their Owner. So He is not questioned about what He does, including choosing and other things, while they are questioned.

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[75–76] ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah are all matters returned.﴾ [al-Hajj: 76].

﴿Allah chooses﴾, i.e., selects: ﴿messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾. That is, there is no denial of His choosing from among humans whomever He wills for His message. And there is no basis for their saying: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾ [Sad: 8]. Abu al-Su'ud said: It is as if the Exalted, when He established His oneness in divinity and negated that anything among things could share in it, made clear that He has servants chosen for the message, through whose responding and being followed one reaches the worship of Him, Mighty and Majestic. Al-Baydawi preceded him with something similar. ﴿Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.﴾ ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾ [al-Hajj: 76], i.e., what they have done and what they will do. ﴿And to Allah are all matters returned﴾ [al-Hajj: 76], i.e., because He is their Owner. So He is not questioned about what He does, including choosing and other things, while they are questioned.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 22, verse 77:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[77] ﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate and worship your Lord and do good that you may succeed.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, bow and prostrate﴾: that is, pray. He expressed prayer by these two, because they are its greatest pillars. Or: humble yourselves before Him, the Exalted, and fall down in prostration to Him alone, not to anything else. ﴿And worship your Lord and do good﴾: that is, seek it out, such as maintaining the ties of kinship, caring for orphans, urging the feeding of the needy, and adorning oneself with noble character. ﴿That you may succeed﴾: that is, so that you may be happy and triumph with Paradise.

Notes:

The first: The scholars did not disagree about the first prostration in this surah. They differed about the second prostration, this one. It is narrated from Umar, Ali, Ibn Umar, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Darda' and Abu Musa that they said: "In al-Hajj there are two prostrations." This was also the view of Ibn al-Mubarak, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Ishaq. What supports it is what was narrated "from Uqbah ibn Amir, who said: I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, are there two prostrations in al-Hajj?' He said: 'Yes, and whoever does not prostrate for them, let him not recite them.'" It was recorded by al-Tirmidhi and Abu Dawud. And from Umar ibn al-Khattab, that he recited Surah al-Hajj and prostrated in it twice, and said: "This surah has been favoured with two prostrations." It was recorded by Malik in al-Muwatta'. A group held that al-Hajj has only one prostration, the first, and that this one is not a prostration; this was the view of al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Sufyan al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah and Malik, based on the evidence that He linked prostration with bowing. This indicates that it is a prostration of prayer, not a prostration of recitation, as stated in Lubab al-Ta'wil. That is, because what is customary in such a case in every verse, where the command to prostrate is linked with bowing, is that it is a command to do what is a pillar of prayer, by induction, such as: ﴿And prostrate, and bow﴾ [Al 'Imran: 43]. And when there is a possibility, the inference falls away.

As for the aforementioned hadith, al-Tirmidhi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: its chain is not strong. Others said the same, as in Sharh al-Hidayah by Ibn al-Humam.

Al-Khafaji said: However, what is found in al-Kashf may be objected to: the truth is that prostration, wherever it is established, is not a consequence of a particular feature of that verse, because the indication of the verse is not restricted to the state of recitation at all. Rather, that is only by the action or saying of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. So there is no barrier to the verse indicating the obligation of prostration in prayer. Nevertheless, prostration is legislated when reciting it, because of the narration established concerning it.

The second: Al-Lubab says: The scholars differed about the number of prostrations of recitation. Al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and most people of knowledge held that they are fourteen prostrations. But al-Shafi'i said: in al-Hajj there are two prostrations, and he dropped the prostration of (Sad). Abu Hanifah said: in al-Hajj there is one prostration, and he affirmed the prostration of (Sad). This was also the view of Ahmad in one of his two narrations. According to him, the prostrations are fifteen. A group held that al-Mufassal has no prostration in it; this is narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn Abbas, and it was the view of Malik.

Accordingly, the prostrations of the Qur'an are eleven. This is indicated by what is narrated from Abu al-Darda', that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There are eleven prostrations in the Qur'an." It was recorded by Abu Dawud, who said: its chain is weak. The evidence of those who say there are fifteen prostrations in the Qur'an is what is narrated "from Amr ibn al-'As, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught me fifteen prostrations in the Qur'an, three of them in al-Mufassal, and in Surah al-Hajj two prostrations." It was recorded by Abu Dawud. And it is authentic from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "We prostrated with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in (Iqra') [al-'Alaq: 1] and (Idha al-sama'u inshaqqat) [al-Inshiqaq: 1]." It was recorded by Muslim. End of quotation.

The fifteen are: in al-A'raf, al-Ra'd, al-Nahl, al-Isra', Maryam, al-Hajj, al-Furqan, al-Naml, Alif Lam Mim Tanzil, Sad, Ha Mim, al-Sajdah, al-Najm, al-Inshiqaq, and Iqra'.

Al-Mufassal, in the most correct opinions, runs from Surah al-Hujurat to the end of the Qur'an. It was named mufassal because of the abundance of separation (fasl) between its surahs.

The third: Prostration of recitation is a sunnah for the reciter and the listener. This is the view of Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, based on the saying of Ibn Umar: "The Prophet ﷺ used to recite to us a surah in which there is a prostration, and he would prostrate, and we would prostrate with him, until one of us could not find a place for his forehead." Narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim).

And Umar said: "Allah has not obligated prostration upon us unless we wish." Narrated by al-Bukhari.

And His saying, exalted is He:

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[78] ﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you, and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion, the creed of your father Abraham. He named you "Muslims" before, and in this [Revelation], so that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish the prayer, give the zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector; how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper!﴾.

﴿And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him﴾ is general, covering striving against the disbelievers, the oppressors, and the self. "Haqqa" (truly, as due) is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdariyyah). The original would be "jihadan fihi haqqan" (striving in Him in a true manner), but the order was reversed, and the "haqq" was made an attribute of "jihad" for emphasis, to indicate that what is required is fulfilling its obligations and conditions in full and complete form, to the extent of one's capacity. On the authority of al-Radi: when "kull" (all), "jadd" (true, real) and "haqq" (true, due) follow a common noun and are attached to a like of their antecedent in wording and meaning, as in "You are a scholar of every scholar" (anta 'alimun kulla 'alimin), or "jadda 'alimin" or "haqqa 'alimin," they indicate that there is gathered in him the qualities that are dispersed among all others, and that whatever else is falsehood or jest. His words, exalted is He, ﴿He has chosen you﴾ mean: He has selected you for His religion and for His support. This contains an indication of the motive for striving and the one who calls to it, because the one who chooses only chooses someone who serves him, and that is what has been mentioned. Also, whoever has been brought near by the Mighty is obliged to repel his enemies and strive against his own self by abandoning what He does not approve.

﴿and has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ means: in all matters of the religion there is no constriction through imposing what is difficult to perform, as was imposed upon those before us. The definite article in "al-din" (the religion) is for comprehensiveness (istighraq). Al-Iklil says: this is the foundation of the principle, "hardship brings facilitation."

﴿the creed of your father Abraham﴾ is in the accusative as a verbal noun, governed by a verb implied by what precedes it, namely the negation of hardship, after deleting a genitive-governing noun; the meaning is: He widened your religion in the manner of the widening of the creed of your father Abraham. Or it is in the accusative by incitement (ighra'), with the implied verb "follow" or "adhere to." Or it is in the accusative by specification (ikhtisas), with the implied "I mean" or the like. Or it is a substitute (badal) or an explicative apposition ('atf bayan) of what precedes it, in which case it would be in the genitive with a fathah, as al-Shihab reported.

Al-Qadi said: He made him their father because he is the father of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he is like a father to his community, in that he is the cause of their eternal life. Or because most of the Arabs were of his descendants, and so they were given precedence over others.

Al-Qashani said: the meaning of his fatherhood is that he was foremost in monotheism, bestowing upon every monotheist, so all of them are his children.

His words, exalted is He, ﴿He named you "Muslims" before﴾ mean: before the revelation of the Qur'an in the earlier scriptures. The clause is independent (mustanafah). It was also said that it is like a substitute for His words, ﴿He has chosen you﴾, and for this reason it is not conjoined with "and." ﴿And in this﴾ means: in the Qur'an. That is: He preferred you over the nations and named you with this most noble name. It was also said that the pronoun refers to Abraham, peace be upon him.

Al-Qadi said: their being named "Muslims" in the Qur'an, though it was not from it, was due to his naming them before, in His words, ﴿and of our descendants a Muslim community for You﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:128], that is, because most of them entered among the descendants; so he was made the namer of them figuratively.

﴿so that the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ means: that he has conveyed to you the messages of your Lord. ﴿and you may be witnesses over the people﴾ means: by the conveying of the messengers the messages of Allah to them. ﴿So establish the prayer, give the zakah, and hold fast to Allah. He is your Protector; how excellent a Protector and how excellent a Helper!﴾ means: since He has singled you out with this honour and preference, worship Him, spend from what He has given you in kindness to the poor and the needy, trust in Him, and seek no support or guardianship except from Him, for He is the best Protector and Helper.
